findings.how_to_check: Run `do MATCHING/check_placebo.do ML` in Stata and observe that the script proceeds to test `link1930_1940_ans_cleaned_noraceblock0.dta` rather than aborting with an invalid argument error.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalize case and explicitly validate the `mode` parameter before setting filenames: `local mode = lower(strtrim(\"`1'\"))` followed by `if !inlist(\"`mode'\", \"\", \"ml\") { display as error \"check_placebo: invalid mode '`1''. Expected empty or 'ml'.\" \n exit 198 }`.
findings.title: Unrecognized or non-lowercase mode argument silently tests the Ancestry baseline instead of failing
findings.what_the_code_does: The script sets the default filenames to the Ancestry baseline at lines 23-24 (`link1930_1940_ans_cleaned_noraceblock0.dta` and `link1930_1940_fsplacebo1930_1940_cleaned_noraceblock0.dta`), and only switches them to the ML files at lines 25-27 under `if \"`mode'\"==\"ml\"`. Any non-empty argument other than exact lower-case `ml`—such as `ML`, `m1`, or `placebo_ml`—silently leaves the filenames pointing to the Ancestry baseline.
findings.why_it_matters: A user who attempts to test the FamilySearch-1930 plus ML-1940 placebo path with an invalid or capitalized mode argument (e.g. `do MATCHING/check_placebo.do ML`) will see the script report `PLACEBO PASSED: identical to link1930_1940_ans_cleaned_noraceblock0.dta`. This provides false assurance that the ML placebo test passed when it was never actually executed.

review_limits: No paper draft was supplied with the review request; claims-vs-code could not be assessed against manuscript text, and the untracked draft reading notes in review/revision-notes-2026-11-13.md are not an executable paper draft.
The multi-gigabyte census and linkage data files on external storage (D:\... and F:\...) are gitignored and not present in the sandbox, so Stata scripts could not be executed at runtime.

Review was diff-scoped to uncommitted working tree changes (MATCHING/check_placebo.do and untracked review/revision-notes-2026-11-13.md); unchanged files in CODE/ and LINKAGE/ were not audited in full.
Stata syntax and macro expansion were evaluated by static source code reading rather than dynamic execution in a live Stata environment.
structured_output.summary: The uncommitted addition of the ML-path placebo comparison in MATCHING/check_placebo.do correctly specifies the expected mixed-vintage link file and rigorously verifies pair-level and attribute-level equivalence against the paper's ML links. The primary defect is that any unrecognized or non-lowercase mode argument silently falls back to running the Ancestry placebo comparison instead of failing, which can give false assurance of ML equivalence if invoked with a typo. Explicit validation of the mode argument should be added before deploying the check.

verified_clean.evidence: MATCHING/check_placebo.do:15,25-28 pairs `link1930_1940_true_cleaned_noraceblock0.dta` with `link1930_1940_fsplacebo1930_ml1940_cleaned_noraceblock0.dta`; the latter matches the dynamic naming logic in `MATCHING/3_append_and_clean_all_links_christian_torbenV2.do:80-82,141` when `fs_years` is 1930, `fstype` is `_fsplacebo_cleaned`, and `ml_years` is 1940.
verified_clean.item: Documented ML matching command produces the exact filenames expected by check_placebo.do.

verified_clean.evidence: MATCHING/check_placebo.do:33,42 runs `isid id_A id_B` on both the baseline paper links and the placebo links, preventing silent many-to-many merge errors.
verified_clean.item: Link pair uniqueness is verified before merging.

verified_clean.evidence: MATCHING/check_placebo.do:47-51 counts `_merge!=3` and sets `bad=1`, which triggers `exit 9` at line 59 if link pairs differ between the two files.
verified_clean.item: Discrepancies in link composition cause the check to halt with an error.

verified_clean.evidence: MATCHING/check_placebo.do:52-56 iterates over `fiveyr_band`, `f_name_A`, `l_name_A`, `f_name_B`, `l_name_B`, `mi1930`, and `mi1940`, requiring zero discrepancies between `v` and `v_paper` among matched records.
verified_clean.item: All relevant matching attributes are checked for exact equality.

verified_clean.evidence: MATCHING/check_placebo.do:53 tests `v != v_paper` for exact identity across two versions of the same file rather than computing cross-source agreement rates, so matching blank strings (`"" != ""` = 0) and missing values (`. != .` = 0) correctly evaluate to parity.
verified_clean.item: Empty string and numeric missing values do not spuriously inflate match parity.

verified_clean.evidence: MATCHING/check_placebo.do:37-38 uses a Stata `tempfile` and modifies no permanent datasets or repository files.

summary.description: Two to four sentences. The overall state of the reviewed work and the single most important thing to fix. No preamble.

dimensions_reviewed.description: Which scope dimensions were actually reviewed in this run.

findings.description: Defects and concerns, ordered most severe first. Empty if none. Do not pad with stylistic observations.

severity.description: blocker: a reported result is wrong. major: a referee would demand it. minor: real but survivable. nit: cosmetic.

confidence.description: verified: traced in the source. likely: strongly implied but depends on unseen data. speculative: a question, not an established defect.

title.description: One line, stating the defect itself, not its category.

location.description: path:line, or path:line-line. Several may be comma-separated. Required: a finding without a location is not a finding.

what_the_code_does.description: Precisely what the code computes, quoting the relevant expression. Contrast with what it was evidently intended to compute.

why_it_matters.description: The consequence for a number or claim in the paper. If there is no consequence, the severity is nit.

how_to_check.description: A concrete command, tabulation, or count the author can run to confirm or refute this in minutes.

suggested_fix.description: The change, specific enough to act on. Do not apply it yourself.

verified_clean.description: Things explicitly checked that were fine. This is what makes a short findings list trustworthy rather than lazy.

evidence.description: How it was confirmed, with path:line where applicable.

review_limits.description: What this review could NOT establish: data not readable, pipeline not runnable, paper text unavailable, Stata semantics not verifiable by reading. Be explicit; silence here reads as false assurance.
